# opencode-cache-manager [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager?label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager) [![ci](https://github.com/noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager)](LICENSE) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager)

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin for managing your prompt cache. Keep the cache of idle sessions warm with hidden pings so they don't expire while you're away. The TUI gives you a way to visualise your cache state and savings from your cache keepalive runs. This plugin is highly configurable and especially tuned for Claude and OpenAI GPT-5.6+. Pick a cache TTL per session (5 minutes, 1 hour, or a hybrid of the two). Pings are timed to land just before it expires. For a short overview with the install steps, see the [OpenCode Cache Manager page](https://toolkit.noppu.com/opencode/opencode-cache-manager) on Noppu Labs' AI Toolkit site.

## Quickstart ```sh opencode plugin add @noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager ``` ## Supported models - It works with Claude and OpenAI models through their official API or through proxies such as OpenRouter or OmniRoute (via Anthropic Messages API or OpenAI-compatible endpoints). - It can work with other models as long as they support Claude/OpenAI style of cache breakpoints, with some [additional configuration](#settings). - For incompatible/unconfigured models (e.g. older GPT, Gemini, or DeepSeek), the plugin shows how much of each prompt was cached and performs no keepalive mechanics (because you'd get no benefit from it). --- ## Contents - [Why](#why) - [The three modes](#the-three-modes) - [Modes per provider](#modes-per-provider) - [Supported providers and endpoints](#supported-providers-and-endpoints) - [Install](#install) - [Usage](#usage) - [Per-model override](#per-model-override) - [Proxies and other provider ids](#proxies-and-other-provider-ids) - [Keepalive](#keepalive) - [Settings](#settings) - [Sidebar](#sidebar) - [Savings](#savings) - [Contributing](#contributing) ## Why OpenCode marks Claude's cache breakpoints on its own (tools, system prompt, the last message) but always sends `ttl: "5m"`, and there is no config option for it. Step away for ten minutes and your next prompt writes the whole context into the cache again at 1.25x the base input price (2x for the 1h cache) instead of reading it at about 0.1x. GPT-5.6+ has the same problem: OpenAI caches for 30 minutes on its own, and the 12-hour cache has to be requested per breakpoint, which OpenCode never does. This plugin rewrites the outgoing request after OpenCode's own cache policy runs, so you can switch a session to the long-lived cache (1 hour on Claude, 12 hours on GPT-5.6+) without forking the provider package. Keepalive handles the other half: it sends a small ping shortly before the cache would expire, so the context is still cached when you come back. Published to npm under two names with identical contents: `@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager` and `opencode-cache-manager`. ## The three modes The modes are named after Claude's cache TTLs; [Modes per provider](#modes-per-provider) maps them onto OpenAI's. On Claude: | Mode | Tools + system | Messages | Write cost | | -------------- | -------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | | `5m` (default) | 5m ephemeral | 5m ephemeral | 1.25x base input | | `1h` | 1h ephemeral | 1h ephemeral | 2x base input | | `hybrid` | 1h ephemeral | 5m ephemeral | mixed | Reads cost about 0.1x base input in every mode. `hybrid` exists because Anthropic requires 1-hour breakpoints to come before any 5-minute ones in a request: the stable prefix (tools + system) gets the long TTL, and the message tail, which changes every turn, stays on the cheaper 5m write. Requests in `1h` or `hybrid` mode also get the `anthropic-beta: extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11` header merged in. ### Modes per provider The same three modes drive both providers. OpenAI caches automatically for 30 minutes (written at 1.25x the input price) and offers 12 hours (2.5x) through a per-breakpoint `ttl`: | Mode | Claude | OpenAI GPT-5.6+ | | -------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `5m` | 5m breakpoints on tools, system and messages | Automatic 30m cache; nothing added to the request | | `1h` | 1h breakpoints everywhere | A 12h breakpoint on the last message or tool output | | `hybrid` | 1h on tools + system, 5m on messages | A 12h breakpoint at the end of the system prompt (on the Responses API before OpenCode 2.3.2, where the system prompt is the `instructions` string, on the first input item, which covers `instructions` and tools too); the message tail keeps the automatic 30m cache | One-off requests (titles and other one-off generate calls) also stop paying for cache writes on OpenAI models: the plugin sends them with caching turned off. Keepalive pings follow the shortest-lived part of the cache: every 25 minutes in `5m` and `hybrid` (the 30m cache and the 30m tail), every 10 hours in `1h`. ## Supported providers and endpoints The plugin handles the Anthropic Messages API (`POST …/messages`), OpenAI Chat Completions (`POST …/chat/completions`) and the OpenAI Responses API (`POST …/responses`). Claude models get the full treatment on the first two (on `/responses` they are only observed), and GPT-5.6+ on the last two. Other models (older GPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, …) manage their own cache, so the plugin only shows how much of each prompt was cached. [docs/SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS.md](docs/SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS.md) covers what the plugin does on each wire, how it decides a model is Claude, the example provider configs, and how each provider caches, with links to their docs. ## Install ### Via CLI ```sh opencode plugin add @noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager ``` ### Manually registered Add the package to the `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. OpenCode installs it at startup: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ "@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager", // or: "opencode-cache-manager" -- same package, unscoped name ], } ``` ### From clone To run from a local clone, see [docs/CONTRIBUTING.md](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md). Upgrading from 0.1.x? See [docs/UPGRADE.md](docs/UPGRADE.md). ## Usage Run `/cache-manager` in the TUI. It's also in the palette as "Cache Manager". With no argument it opens a picker with a Session section (only shown inside a session) and a Global section:

Session rows that show `· global` inherit the global value; a row without it has a session override. Picking a row opens a list of values, and the numeric settings also offer "Custom…" for a typed value. With an argument, the command edits the **current session only**, never the global settings: ``` /cache-manager 5m -> session TTL mode 5m /cache-manager 1h -> session TTL mode 1h /cache-manager hybrid -> session TTL mode hybrid /cache-manager keepalive on|off -> turn keepalive on or off for this session /cache-manager pings 3 -> at most 3 pings per idle stretch (0-100) /cache-manager min 50k -> minimum context size to ping (50000 or 50k) /cache-manager savings on|off -> show or hide the savings rows for this session /cache-manager reset -> drop the session's overrides /cache-manager status -> toast with the session's effective settings ``` Typed arguments need an open session. Global settings are changed from the picker's Global section or in the plugin options (see [Settings](#settings)). Session overrides and global settings persist in plugin storage across restarts. The server side registers the same command, so explicit arguments also work headless; the reply is posted as a synthetic message instead of a toast. With no argument the server-side command toggles the session's TTL mode between `5m` and `1h`. ### Per-model override Model variants can force a TTL regardless of the session or global mode, via the `x-cache-ttl` sentinel header: ```jsonc "variants": [ { "id": "high", "settings": { "reasoningEffort": "high" } }, { "id": "high-1h", "settings": { "reasoningEffort": "high" }, "headers": { "x-cache-ttl": "1h" } } ] ``` The plugin reads the header before the request goes out, applies that TTL, and strips the header. The [example configs](docs/SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS.md#endpoints) are full provider configs with `-1h` variants; the Anthropic one covers four Claude models. On OpenAI GPT-5.6+ the same header selects the 12h cache. ### Proxies and other provider ids Requests to the `anthropic` and `omniroute-anthropic` providers are always treated as Claude and rewritten automatically. If you reach a model through a proxy registered under another provider id, the plugin recognises the wire by the request: `POST …/messages` is the Anthropic wire, `POST …/chat/completions` is the OpenAI Chat wire, and `POST …/responses` is the OpenAI Responses wire (see [Supported providers and endpoints](docs/SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS.md)). On the Messages wire, and on the OpenAI wires with `openaiCompatible` on, any other provider id is classified by model: a `cacheProfiles` entry, a model name that contains `claude` or starts with `anthropic/`, or the model the latest response reported, applied from the next request. A router alias that switches models therefore runs one turn behind, and on the Messages wire a request such an alias rejects (status 400 or 422) drops what was learned. A non-Claude model on an Anthropic-compatible endpoint (DeepSeek, Kimi, MiniMax, GLM, a router) is observed only: its requests are not rewritten and it is never pinged. The `x-cache-ttl` header forces a TTL only on models classified as Claude or GPT-5.6+; to force it on an alias, map the alias with `cacheProfiles` (see [Upgrading from 0.5.x](docs/UPGRADE.md#from-05x)). Keepalive and the sidebar work with any provider on any wire, since they only need the cache usage in the response. ## Keepalive Keepalive sends a hidden request shortly before a session's cache expires. The request reads the cached prefix, which restarts the TTL. A ping costs roughly one cache read of the session's context, far less than the cold rewrite you pay once the cache is gone. The ping is a transient request that uses the session's context. Nothing is added to the conversation history, and the model is told to reply `OK` without using tools. It reuses the exact conversation bytes of the session's last agent request, so it hits the cache even when other plugins rewrite the history. Those bytes stay in memory and are never written to disk. On a 5m cache the ping goes out 4 minutes after the last request; on a 1h cache, 50 minutes after it. `hybrid` follows the 5m schedule on Claude, because its message tail is cached for 5 minutes. On OpenAI it is 25 minutes in `5m` and `hybrid` (the automatic 30m cache, and in `hybrid` the 30m tail after the 12h prefix) and 10 hours in `1h`. A ping is itself a request, so it restarts the clock and the next ping is scheduled the same way. Any real request on the session (your prompt, a tool-loop request, compaction) cancels the pending ping and resets the ping count to 0. After `maxPings` pings (default 5) in one idle stretch, keepalive stops and the cache expires. Failed pings count towards the limit. A ping is never sent after the cache would have expired; a failed ping is retried after 30 seconds, but only if it can still land before the original expiry. A ping that reads at least 90% of the context from cache is a hit. If it reads less, it's a miss, and keepalive stops for that session until the next real request, so a provider that doesn't reuse the cache can't turn into a stream of paid pings. Keepalive skips: - subagent (child) sessions - sessions waiting on a tool call, such as a running subagent or a long build; they are pinged again once the next request has gone out - sessions whose context is below `minContextTokens` (default 50,000) - sessions with keepalive turned off - sessions where no cache activity has been seen, such as sessions on models without prompt caching All eligible top-level sessions are kept warm at once, not only the one in view. A schedule survives OpenCode reloading the plugin (a config save, for example) and restarting, as long as the cache has not expired in the meantime: the next ping goes out at its original time, and pings already used still count. The conversation bytes a ping reuses are never stored, so pings after a reload use the session's context as OpenCode assembles it until the session's next request. That reads the cache just as well unless another plugin rewrites the history, in which case the first such ping can miss and keepalive stops for the session (`stopped · last ping missed`) until its next request. **Detected TTL.** The schedule uses the TTL the provider actually granted, read from the cache-write breakdown in the response usage. Some providers (for example Claude Code-backed ones) grant 1h regardless of the mode requested. If a response has both 5m and 1h writes, the shorter one wins. Reads don't change the TTL. When the provider gives no breakdown, the requested mode is used. The sidebar labels the source as `detected` or `requested`. > **Pings cost tokens.** Each one is a real provider request that reads the whole context from cache. Keepalive saves money when you come back after a long gap and stay within the ping limit; it costs money for sessions you never return to. > **Don't combine this with OpenCode's built-in `warming: true`.** Both would ping the same session, so you would pay for double the pings. Use one or the other. ## Settings Plugin options set the defaults. They live in the plugin entry in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "@noppu-labs/opencode-cache-manager", "options": { "defaultMode": "1h", "keepalive": { "enabled": true, // default true "maxPings": 5, // default 5 "minContextTokens": 50000, // default 50000 }, "savings": true, // default true "modelsDevPrices": false, // default false "openaiCompatible": true, // default true "cacheProfiles": { "opus": "anthropic", "gpt": "implicit" }, "debug": false, // default false }, }, ], } ``` | Option | Default | Meaning | | ---------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `defaultMode` | `"5m"` | TTL mode when nothing else is set | | `keepalive.enabled` | `true` | Whether keepalive runs | | `keepalive.maxPings` | `5` | Pings per idle stretch | | `keepalive.minContextTokens` | `50000` | Smallest context worth pinging | | `savings` | `true` | Show the `saved` and `return` rows and the ping cost in the sidebar. The ledger keeps counting while hidden. Also in the picker and as `/cache-manager savings on\|off` | | `modelsDevPrices` | `false` | Price models the OpenCode catalog has no price for from models.dev (see [Savings](#savings)). Off means no network calls of the plugin's own. Read at startup; not in the picker | | `openaiCompatible` | `true` | Handle OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses requests. `false` leaves them untouched, except that a model variant's `x-cache-ttl` header is still applied and stripped | | `cacheProfiles` | `{}` | Which cache profile manages a model, by pattern (see below) | | `debug` | `false` | Write a debugging trace to a file (see [Debug log](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#debug-log)). Not in the picker | `cacheProfiles` maps a pattern to a profile. Patterns are matched against `/`, in order, and the first match wins: - `"opus"` is a case-insensitive substring match. - `"/^my-proxy\\/(opus|sonnet)/i"` is a regex: `/body/flags`. The value is one of three profiles: - `"anthropic"`: managed as Claude (TTL rewrite, breakpoints, keepalive). - `"openai"`: managed as OpenAI GPT-5.6+ (12h breakpoints, caching off for one-off calls, keepalive). Only use it for models that accept `prompt_cache_breakpoint`; older ones answer 400. - `"implicit"`: observed only (sidebar `cached` row), never rewritten or pinged. `"gpt": "implicit"` keeps every model with `gpt` in its name out of management. Entries that are empty, aren't valid regexes or name another profile are ignored. Patterns win over the built-in name check and over what the plugin has learned from responses. They apply on the OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses wires. Both options aren't in the picker and have no typed command; they're read at startup. The effective value of each setting is the first one set, in this order: 1. the session's override (`/cache-manager` typed argument, or the picker's Session section) 2. the global value stored from the picker's Global section 3. the plugin option (`defaultMode`, `keepalive.*` or `savings`) 4. the built-in default A global value stored from the picker overrides the plugin option for the same setting, so changing `defaultMode` in `opencode.jsonc` has no effect once the picker has stored a global value for that setting. Changes take effect immediately. Turning keepalive off cancels the pending ping, and lowering `pings` to or below the pings already used ends the run. A TTL mode change is picked up by the next request. The `x-cache-ttl` model-variant header (see [Per-model override](#per-model-override)) still wins over the session mode for the requests it is on. ## Sidebar Inside a session, the sidebar shows a Cache section. It ticks once a second from timestamps the server sends, so countdowns stay live without server traffic. ``` Cache • status warm cached 92% · 141k / 153k expires 14:52 (52m) ttl 1h (detected) next ping 14:42 (42m) pings 2/5 ✓ hit ($0.05) saved $0.42 · 2 rewrites return 9× ping cost ``` - `status` is `warm` with a green bullet, amber once the pings are used up, and `expired` with a red bullet once the cache has expired (then `expired 12m ago` replaces the `expires` row). - `expires` is the clock time and time left until the cache expires. - `ttl` is the TTL being scheduled and where it came from (`detected` or `requested`). OpenAI's usage doesn't say which lifetime it granted, so OpenAI sessions always show `(requested)`, as `30m` or `12h`. Before the first response the section reads `waiting for first response`; so does a session with no armed ping right after a restart, until its next response. - `cached` describes the latest primary turn: the share of its prompt that was read from cache, then the tokens read / the prompt total, such as `92% · 14.8k / 16.1k`. Pings, titles and other one-off requests don't change it. It shows for every session with cache usage, Claude or not, once a response has arrived. - `next ping` is when the next ping goes out. It reads `none` once the limit is reached. - `pings 2/5` counts pings used in this idle stretch, followed by the last result: `✓ hit`, `✗ miss` or `✗ failed`. No result is shown before the first ping. - `pings` also shows what the pings of the current idle stretch cost, such as `($0.05)`, when every ping in the session was priced. - `saved` and `return` are the session's savings totals; see [Savings](#savings). - When keepalive isn't running, a `keepalive` row says why: `off · 31k < 50k` (context below the minimum), `off · disabled`, `waiting · session busy` (waiting on a tool call), or `stopped · last ping missed`. Every other state the section can show:

For a model with an implicit cache (anything that isn't Claude, see [Supported providers and endpoints](docs/SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS.md)) there's no TTL or expiry to show, so the section is the `cached` row and a keepalive row: ``` Cache cached 92% · 14.8k / 16.1k keepalive n/a · implicit cache ``` A Claude Agent session (the `claude-agent` provider) runs through the `claude` CLI, which manages its own cache, so the plugin can't change the TTL or send pings. The section shows what it can read: ```text Cache • status managed by Claude Code cached 84% · 27.7k / 32.8k ttl 1h (detected) ``` The section is hidden for subagent sessions and for sessions with no cache activity. ### Savings Below `pings`, the sidebar shows what keepalive has saved in this session. The first ping creates the rows; before that they are absent. They are also absent for implicit-cache models, which are never pinged. A rewrite counts as saved when all three hold: - at least one ping in the idle stretch was a hit; - your next prompt (or a compaction) came more than 30 seconds after the cache would have expired without pings; - that request read at least 90% of the context from cache. Anything else is ping cost only: a session you never came back to, a return before the cache would have expired, a return after it expired anyway, a return on a different model, which usually doesn't read the old cache. The count errs low on purpose; when a case is unclear, it counts less. The avoided amount is what writing the cached tokens at the stretch's TTL would have cost, minus what reading them cost. On `hybrid`, only the message tail would have expired, so only the tokens past the long-lived prefix count. A stretch that crosses a restart still counts if its ping was armed at the time; otherwise its return isn't counted. Pings already paid stay paid, and after a restart a session's totals reappear after its next request. - `saved` is the session total. In dollars it is net: avoided cost minus the cost of every ping, wasted ones included. Without a price it is `2 rewrites · 282k`, the rewrites and the tokens they avoided. `saved nothing yet` shows once you've paid for a ping and nothing has been saved. - `return` is avoided cost divided by ping cost, such as `9× ping cost`. It appears after the first save. The label may change. Dollars need a price for every model the session used. OpenCode's catalog prices the models of known providers. For a model under a custom provider, add `cost` to the model in `opencode.jsonc` (`input`, `output`, `cache.read`, `cache.write`, in dollars per million tokens; `cache.write` prices 5m and 30m writes, while 1h and 12h writes are priced from `input` at 2x and 2.5x); [the OpenAI-compatible example](docs/examples/opencode.openai-compatible.jsonc) shows where. Or set `modelsDevPrices` to `true` to look up models the catalog has no price for in models.dev. That is the only network call the plugin makes, once a day at most (within one run of OpenCode, a failed fetch is retried after 15 minutes at the earliest; that wait isn't kept across restarts), and a price from there is the list price at the model's base tier, with no long-context tier, which may differ from what a subscription-backed route charges you. A failed lookup, or a model with no clear match, leaves the model unpriced. If OpenCode's model catalog can't be loaded, events are unpriced and models.dev is not consulted. If any event in a session has no price, the whole session shows the unit-free form, since a partial dollar figure would mislead. Each event is priced with the model that served it, so a session that switches models still adds up. Dollar amounts round to the cent, with `<$0.01` for a non-zero amount below a cent and a minus sign (`-$0.02`) for a negative net. Turn the rows off with `savings` in the plugin options, in the picker, or with `/cache-manager savings off` for one session. The ledger keeps counting while they are hidden. Totals are kept when a session becomes implicit. Totals of deleted sessions are removed at the next startup. ## Contributing See [docs/CONTRIBUTING.md](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) for the local setup, the checks CI runs and how releases are cut. --- Maintained by [Noppu Labs](https://noppu.com).
